āpaṇa.notes: The DPPN entry explicitly covers both DPD examples. SN 48.50 calls Āpaṇa a town of the Aṅgas. MN 54, MN 66 and the parallel Sela accounts in MN 92 and Snp 3.7 call it a town of the Aṅguttarāpans. The citation list misses Snp 3.7 and picks up neighboring MN 53, MN 65, MN 91, MN 93 and SN 48.49, all of which lack a mention of the town.

ārāmadaṇḍa.notes: In the app, Ārāmadaṇḍa questions Mahākaccāna at Varaṇā in AN 2.37. DPD gives AN 2.38, where the questioner is Kandarāyana. DPPN's account gives sensual desire as the cause of both quarrels. AN 2.37 distinguishes attachment to sensual desire among laypeople from attachment to views among ascetics. At the end Ārāmadaṇḍa asks Mahākaccāna to remember him as a lay follower after taking refuge in Gotama, the Dhamma and the Saṅgha. The Pali setting reads bhaddasāritīre where DPPN and Sujato name Kaddama.

ātumā.notes: The citation list is empty despite DPPN's reference to DN ii 131–132. At DN 16:4.30 the Buddha tells Pukkusa he was in a threshing hut at Ātumā when the storm killed two brothers and four oxen.

īsāna.notes: DN 13 includes Īsāna among the gods invoked by brahmins. SN 11.3 names him as a king of gods with a banner. DPPN's further claim that he commanded a division goes beyond what the battle account says.
